name: java-springboot
description: Best practices for high-quality Spring Boot applications.

Use Maven (`pom.xml`) or Gradle (`build.gradle`) for dependency management and Spring Boot starters (e.g., `spring-boot-starter-web`, `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa`). Organize by feature/domain (e.g., `com.example.app.order`, `com.example.app.user`), not layer. Always use constructor-based injection for required dependencies; declare dependency fields `private final`. Use `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, and `<REDACTED_USER>`/`<REDACTED_USER>` annotations appropriately.

Use `application.yml` (or `application.properties`); prefer YAML. Use `<REDACTED_USER>` for type-safe properties. Use Spring Profiles (`application-dev.yml`, `application-prod.yml`). Do not hardcode secrets. Use environment variables or HashiCorp Vault/AWS Secrets Manager.

Design consistent RESTful endpoints. Use DTOs; Do not expose JPA entities directly to the client. Use Java Bean Validation (JSR 380) with (`<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`) on DTOs. Implement global exception handling with `<REDACTED_USER>` and `<REDACTED_USER>`. Encapsulate all business logic within `<REDACTED_USER>` classes; services should be stateless. Use `<REDACTED_USER>` on service methods for declarative transactions, at the most granular level necessary.

Use Spring Data JPA repositories extending `JpaRepository` or `CrudRepository`. For complex queries, use `<REDACTED_USER>` or JPA Criteria API. Use DTO projections. Use SLF4J:
`private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MyClass.class);`
Use parameterized messages (`logger.info("Processing user {}...", userId);`), not concatenation.
